stories.summary:
I enjoy putting the pedal to the metal, pen to the paper, peanut butter to jel.. ok I'll shut up. Predictions are fun because your either right or you are the dumbest person alive. I yearly go through all 272 games through nfl playoff predictor and predict out the season. This is where I ended up, but please comment or share your prediction:



	 



	AFC



	1. CIN (AFCN) 13-4



	2. DEN (AFCW) 12-5



	3. HOU (AFCS) 11-6



	4. BUF (AFCE) 11-6



	5. KC 12-5



	6. NE 11-6



	7. JAX 10-7



	Just missed: BAL 10-7 miss on tiebreaker, IND 9-8 // LAC 8-9 



	 



	I am buying the koolaid that CIN finally is back and I truly do believe their defense has done enough to be middle of the road which gets them back not only into the playoffs but tops of the AFC. I review & analyze teams schedules pretty deep and one of the things that helps catapult a team to a great year is a favorable schedule (as NE proved last year). Even playing in the AFC North the Bengals schedule is incredibly favorable this year which bolds well. DEN I have been high on all off season and even with two more losses they beat out KC for the division. HOU wins the division again as the defense is great and offense better where it can do things. I truly think the Bills season is a tight one throughout with NE and we get them on tiebreakers this time. I also think it won't be until the last third of the season the defense comes together so if they start 4-3 I am not panicking. The Chiefs return to the dance as variance favors them this year after a year of everything going wrong & Mahomes is too good for them to miss again. NE takes a step back record wise but frankly has a better team. JAX proves their real despite a tough schedule and makes back to back playoff appearances for the first time in two decades.



	 



	The Ravens are the odd man out as they have a good year but lose on tiebreakers. I think it will take a year for the defense to come together, their offensive line is not nearly as settled as people say, and my bold prediction of the year is Henry finally meets father time which slows their offense down. Like Seattle in 2024 the foundation is set for the future though and BAL comes into 2027 far scarier. IND hangs around but can't finish the deal and the Chargers losses on defense are too much for an offense that always has injuries.



	 



	NFC



	1. LAR (NFCW) 13-4



	2. DAL (NFCE) 13-4



	3. DET (NFCN) 12-5



	4. CAR (NFCS) 9-8



	5. PHI 12-5



	6. SEA 12-5



	7. MIN 10-7



	Just missed: GB 10-7 miss on tiebreaker, CHI 9-8 // SF 9-8 // NOLA 9-8



	 



	The Rams exact revenge on Seattle to clinch the 1 seed and division this year as Seattle falls to the 6 seed despite a 12-5 campaign. Dallas sees their investment on defense pay off big time and the offense goes rough shot to miss the 1 seed due to tiebreaker as they lose to the Rams. DET was a playoff team based on advanced stats last year but luck, injuries, and turnovers hurt them; not this year as the 4th place schedule gifts them an easy run for the division. The NFC South sucks but someone needs to win and I buy the Panthers especially on defense even with injury to do enough an beat NOLA on a tiebreaker at 9-8. My bold prediction in the NFC is Tampa Bay implodes losing their last five after starting 6-6 and they proceed to clean house. PHI misses the division but still makes it in as a Wild Card. Minnesota has quality QB play that jolts them past Green Bay who I think is stuck as a middling team that is can win 9-11 games but not enough to be more. CHI great offense but the defense lacks talent & doesn't get turnovers this year while San Fran losses the gamble against father time and the age of their stars catches them with injuries again and they miss.



	 



	~Please note I am wayyyy more confident in my regular season picks & field vs what happens in the postseason~



	 



	Playoffs



	AFC Wild Card: 2. DEN losses to 7. JAX  //  3. HOU defeats 6. NE  //  4. BUF defeats 5. KC 



	NFC Wild Card: 2. DAL defeats to 7. MIN  //  3. DET losses to 6. SEA  //  4. CAR losses to 5. PHI



	 



	AFC Divisional: 1. CIN losses to 7. JAX  //  3. HOU loses to 4. BUF 



	NFC Divisional: 1. LAR defeats 6.SEA  //   2. DAL defeats to 5. PHI 



	 



	AFC Title: 4. BUF defeats 7. JAX



	NFC Title: 1. LAR defeats 2. DAL



	 



	Super Bowl: 4. BUF defeats 1. LAR



	 



	No time like the present eh. Buffalo eviscerates playoff pain against KC to land a rematch against HOU who they lost narrowly to week 1. This time the Bills defense can dictate enough on their side to allow the Bills offense to a play a very rope a dope game that is borrowing as hell but fails to give HOU mistakes to capitalize on. The Bills get the tough Jags at home, but thanks to some favorable weather causing a Trevor Lawrence fumble with ten to go the Bills out last them 24-21.



	 



	The Rams as the 1 seed avoid the chaos of the NFC for a week before an all time classic vs Seattle as Stafford gets Adams on a last second TD. Dallas makes a run to the NFC title for the first time since 1996, but LA's defense is too much for the Cowboys and the Rams offense puts the game out of hand in the 4th quarter.



	 



	Super Bowl: Bills over Rams 27-23. The Bills win the rematch after they fell early in the season 30-24. The Bills defense and offense are a bit more unified compared to early season growing pains, whereas the length of the season on the Rams aging stars catches up just enough where the Bills can land enough blows on defense to allow Josh & the offense to stay ahead for the title.

stories.title: Texans' GM  Nick Caserio's Assessment of the Bills and DETAILED Discussion of Josh Allen
stories.summary:
Again, he didn't give any bulletin materials, but one or two sentences description of every starter is something I have not seen from opposing GMs on our roster. You can sort of tell he provides more description on our better players and the others he just wipes thru like "a compliment player." I started the video below from the question asked about Stroud because I want to hear his assessment of CJ, then it goes right into the questions and answers on the Bills and Allen. 



	 



	A few notes:



	
		On Stroud, he said having the best training camp so far in his career. Not much after that. Of course the hosts are not going to mention those playoff performance, presumanly it has been asked and talked to death in the off-season. 
	
	
		He gave Beane high praises, "one of the best General Managers in all football." I'd imagine Beane would be a highly desirable commodity if he's ever let go by the Bills.
	
	
		Sounds like he's in on Leonhard too, "always ... a highly thought of assistant coach."
	
	
		DJ Moore, "very consistant, very productive, very durable player."
	
	
		On defensive, the first player he mentioned is Deone Walker, "looks like he's made a lot of progress." 
	
	
		Sounds like he's pretty high on Chubb's acquisition.
	
	
		Also mentioned KEO having a good camp. Probably the only non starter he noted.
	
	
		On specific question of Josh Allen, very elaborate description of what Allen presents to an opponent. Good to hear an active non-Bills personnel chief describes it.
	



	 



	Overall, he's pretty much plugged in on what is going on in Bills land. You can bet every play we ran in open camp or pre-season games, who was on which personal grouping, they probably have all of that. Still, there is a lot of guessing on what Leonhard will trout out on Sept. 13 but they will have a pretty accurate idea what we may do in general.

stories.title: Now that the 53 is set, predict the Bills win total (2026 Edition)
stories.summary:
Now that we know the initial 53-man roster, and the practice squad is set, it's prediction time.  This is the time every year that I make my one (1) prediction for the Bills regular season.  My track record is pretty good - I'm generally +/- 1 win from the Bills' actual total.  (Last year I hit it exact.)



	 



	I don't go game-by-game; instead I try to look holistically at the Bills as a team for the full season.  I do take overall strength of schedule into account, but upsets happen both ways, so I think it's futile to predict the results of each week well in advance.  Likewise, injuries happen, guys have big games here and there, etc.  There's some averaging out, but overall a really good team tends to win more than a fairly good team, which tends to win more than a mediocre team, and so on.



	 



	So with that preamble aside, I'll go on record:  I'm predicting 12 wins from the Bills this year.  I have way better vibes going in to this season, but the new players and schemes will need some time to gel, and the schedule is very tough.

Vince Young Documentary on Netflix
stories.summary:
Watched the Vince Young Documentary on Netflix.....actually forgot he was on the Bills roster for a hot minute.



	 



	Obviously he was super talented, and he seems to have a decent level of intelligence......but as you will see when you watch it, what he lacked was emotional toughness.



	 



	One person who came off pretty bad in the Doc was Coach Jeff Fisher.



	 



	I believe Barry Switzer once said the most important job for a Coach is to figure out which players need a kick in the butt, and which players need a pat on the back, and act accordingly.



	 



	Vince Young seemed to be a player that needed a pat on the back, but all he got from Fisher were kicks in the butt.



	 



	Sad that Young seemed to have all the physical tools and intelligence to be great, but if you look into his family history and his behavior in his early days at Texas, any decent GM should've been able to spot the red flags that would lead you to believe he wouldn't be able to cut it on the Pro level.
